title: Composition of derived pullbacks
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] (more generally of ringed spaces). There is a canonical natural isomorphism $Lf^*\circ Lg^*\cong L(g\circ f)^*$ of functors $D(\mathcal O_Z)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], with derived pullback as in [def-pc-derived-pullback]. These isomorphisms are unital ($L(\mathrm{id}_X)^*\cong\mathrm{id}$, compatibly with the composition isomorphisms) and associative: for a further morphism $h:W\to X$ the two resulting isomorphisms $Lh^*\circ Lf^*\circ Lg^*\cong L(g\circ f\circ h)^*$ coincide.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] (applied to the site of open subsets of $Z$ with the sheaf of rings $\mathcal O_Z$), choose a K-flat complex $K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules with a quasi-isomorphism $K^\bullet\to E$ on $Z$. By [def-pc-derived-pullback], $Lg^*E$ is represented by $g^*K^\bullet$; by [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation] this is K-flat on $Y$, so applying [def-pc-derived-pullback] again represents $Lf^*Lg^*E$ by $f^*g^*K^\bullet$. The canonical underived pullback identification $f^*g^*K^\bullet\cong(g\circ f)^*K^\bullet$ is termwise the associativity of tensor products, hence identifies this complex with $L(g\circ f)^*E$. The termwise maps commute with chain maps, so they are natural in $E$ and give the claimed canonical natural isomorphism.

For an identity morphism, the displayed comparison is the canonical unitor of the derived tensor construction, hence $L(\mathrm{id}_X)^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and the comparison is compatible with composition. For composable $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, and $h:W\to X$, the two comparisons from $Lf^*\circ Lg^*\circ Lh^*$ to $L(g\circ f\circ h)^*$ are the two reassociations of the same fourfold tensor product. Mac Lane associativity for tensor products makes these reassociations equal, so the composition isomorphisms satisfy the unit and associativity coherence laws.
